title: Dividing by sharing equally
keyIdea: Dividing means sharing fairly into equal groups.

kid: Dividing means sharing fairly, so every group gets the same. 12 grapes shared between 3 friends gives 4 each: 12 ÷ 3 = 4.
It can also mean 'how many groups of 3 can I make from 12?' The answer is 4 again.
adult: Division has two meanings: sharing (12 into 3 groups: how many in each?) and grouping (how many 3s fit into 12?). Both give 12 ÷ 3 = 4.
Division undoes multiplication (3 × 4 = 12). The 'equal shares' idea is exactly what fractions build on: 1/3 of 12 is one of three equal shares.

familyTip: Share snacks out 'one for you, one for me' and ask whether it came out fair. Try amounts that don't share evenly, too.

practice.prompt: {=a*b} grapes are shared fairly between {a} children. How many grapes does each child get?
practice.hint: Give one each in turn until they run out.

practice.prompt: How many groups of 4 can you make from 8 cupcakes?
practice.hint: Keep taking 4 away until none are left.

practice.explain: The shares are different sizes. Fair sharing of 9 between 3 would give 3 each.
